helpers.name: scan_source_tree

parameters.name: module_path
parameters.description: Project-relative subtree to narrow the scan to (e.g. 'src/aimfp/helpers/project'). Defaults to the whole source_directory. Use this to adopt a large codebase one module at a time.

parameters.name: include_nested
parameters.description: Include functions defined inside other functions

parameters.name: untracked_only
parameters.description: Report only files with no existing database record. Use on re-scans to see just what is new.

helpers.purpose: Read-only inventory of an existing codebase for adoption into AIMFP tracking. Walks source_directory applying the watchdog's exact exclusion stack (built-in exclusions + watchdog_excluded_* settings + .watchdogignore), extracts signatures, and reports tracked vs untracked. Writes nothing — review the inventory, then register with catalog_files/catalog_functions/catalog_types.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if the scan path does not exist. Files that fail to parse are reported in parse_failures rather than aborting the scan; unreadable or unsupported-extension files are reported in skipped_unsupported.
return_statements: SCAN IS READ-ONLY — nothing was written. Review the inventory, enrich purposes where extraction left them null, then register via catalog_files first (functions and types need file_id).

ORDER MATTERS: catalog_files → capture returned IDs → catalog_functions and catalog_types using those file_ids → then compose the existing batch tools: add_files_to_module, add_file_flows, add_interactions, add_types_functions.

FIDELITY: files with fidelity='full' (Python) carry real parameters and returns. Files with fidelity='names_only' carry names and line numbers only — you MUST supply purpose, parameters, and returns yourself before cataloging, or the entries will be invisible to future lookup.
Large result sets: narrow with module_path and catalog one module at a time rather than registering hundreds of functions in a single pass.

If total_files is large and untracked_files equals it, this is a first-time adoption. Confirm the codebase is FP-compliant before cataloging — AIMFP rejects OOP codebases, and cataloging one commits you to tracking code the FP directives will fight.

used_by_directives.description: Build the file inventory with extracted signatures before any registration

helpers.name: scan_call_graph

parameters.name: module_path
parameters.description: Project-relative subtree to limit analysis to. Only the CALLING side is narrowed — functions outside it still resolve as targets, so cross-module edges are never lost.

helpers.purpose: Build the interaction graph for already-cataloged functions: which tracked function calls which. Read-only — returns tuples shaped for add_interactions, which does the writing. Run AFTER catalog_files and catalog_functions. Resolution is conservative and strictest-first (explicit import, then same-file, then module alias, then project-wide unique name), following re-export chains through modules that define no functions of their own. Ambiguous targets are dropped and counted rather than guessed at, because a wrong edge sends future refactors chasing dependencies that do not exist.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if no tracked functions exist (catalog files and functions first). Files that fail to parse are skipped rather than aborting the scan. Non-Python files are skipped — call graph extraction requires ast.
return_statements: READ-ONLY — nothing was written. Pass the returned 'interactions' straight to add_interactions to persist the graph. Batch in chunks of a few hundred for large codebases.

Review 'resolved_by': edges resolved by 'unique_name' are the weakest class (matched only because the name happens to be unique project-wide). A high 'unique_name' share relative to 'import'/'local'/'reexport' suggests imports the resolver could not follow — worth a spot check.
'unresolved_count' greater than zero means real call edges were dropped as ambiguous. Inspect 'unresolved_sample' and add those interactions manually if they matter.
Python only. A polyglot codebase gets no edges for its non-Python files — record those interactions manually or leave the graph partial knowingly.
After writing interactions, link types to functions via add_types_functions to complete the index.

used_by_directives.description: Recover the dependency graph after files and functions are registered

helpers.name: catalog_files

parameters.name: files
parameters.description: Array of {name, path, language} objects. 'path' is project-relative and is the identity key.

helpers.purpose: Register existing files in project.db in a single phase. For code already on disk: rows are written finalized (is_reserved=0) with ID naming off, because existing filenames are fixed and cannot carry an _id_ suffix. Use INSTEAD OF reserve_files/finalize_files when adopting an existing codebase. Idempotent on path.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error on an empty list or a record missing 'path'. Atomic — all records commit or none do. An already-tracked path is updated in place, never duplicated.
return_statements: Files registered. IDs are returned in input order — map them back to your scan results to build the file_id for each function and type.
NEXT: catalog_functions and catalog_types for these files. A cataloged file with 0 tracked functions is incomplete unless it is data-only or config-only.
THEN: assign to modules via add_files_to_module and to flows via add_file_flows. A file with 0 flow assignments is architecturally disconnected.
created_count vs updated_count tells you whether this was a first catalog or a re-scan refresh.

used_by_directives.description: Single-phase registration of scanned files, replacing the reserve/finalize pair for existing code

helpers.name: catalog_functions

parameters.name: functions
parameters.description: Array of {name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns} objects. 'parameters' is a list of param dicts and 'returns' a dict; both are JSON-encoded on write.

helpers.purpose: Register existing functions in project.db in a single phase. Use INSTEAD OF reserve_functions/finalize_functions when adopting an existing codebase. Idempotent on (file_id, name), so a re-scan after source changes refreshes signatures instead of duplicating them.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error on an empty list or a record missing 'name' or 'file_id'. Atomic — all records commit or none do.
return_statements: Functions registered. Verify purpose, parameters, and returns are populated — entries with null fields cannot be looked up by signature in future sessions and reduce the DB to a name index.

BLOCKED until interactions are mapped: for every cataloged function that calls another tracked function, record it via add_interactions. A cataloged codebase with zero interactions has no dependency graph, which is most of the value.
TYPES: link cataloged functions to the types they consume or produce via add_types_functions.
Functions extracted at fidelity='names_only' arrive with empty parameters and returns — fill these in rather than leaving them null.

used_by_directives.description: Single-phase registration of extracted function signatures

helpers.name: catalog_types

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Array of {name, file_id, definition, description} objects. 'definition' is a dict describing the type shape and is JSON-encoded on write.

helpers.purpose: Register existing type definitions in project.db in a single phase. Use INSTEAD OF reserve_types/finalize_types when adopting an existing codebase. Idempotent on (file_id, name).
helpers.error_handling: Returns error on an empty list, a record missing 'name', or a record with neither 'definition' nor 'definition_json'. Atomic — all records commit or none do.
return_statements: Types registered. Verify definition and description are populated — types are the most frequently looked-up entities, and incomplete entries force the full file reads the DB exists to eliminate.
NEXT: link these types to the functions that use them via add_types_functions, so 'what functions use TypeX?' and refactoring impact analysis work.

used_by_directives.description: Single-phase registration of extracted type definitions
